title: Chloe Thinking Studio · film evaluation
target: NSW selective high school placement test in 2027 for Year 7 entry in 2028
subject: Thinking Skills
voice: Australian Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS (Chloe Sydney Logic Tutor AU)

lessons.title: How to use Thinking Studio
lessons.observation: The sun leads the leaf in more than one legal placement; a pencil and the next-day card support the try/return routine.

lessons.title: A parent’s guide to lasting learning
lessons.observation: Both complete race examples put Ari before Bo, first with a gap then next to Bo. This illustrates testing a must or exhibiting a could.

lessons.title: Follow the guarantee
lessons.observation: The card approaches the reader, the barrier lifts, and a covered input can still leave the barrier open. This supplies a forward instance and leaves the card in the last case undetermined.
lessons.questionReview: Recognition of a trigger licenses its guaranteed result. The robotics/bus prediction and two label/machine questions require forward inference.

lessons.title: Required or enough?
lessons.observation: Mia delivers a form. Jin and Tess can be named as finalists with completed forms while Mia’s form remains visible and her result is undecided.
lessons.questionReview: A required test time alone cannot settle relay selection. Lab access and exhibition display contrast a requirement with an independently sufficient condition.

lessons.title: Decode “only if”
lessons.observation: Nina moves across the gate synced dynamically to the Australian narration in c3-cross; c3-stay preserves her wristband while changing whether she enters; Room B distinguishes no permitted use from knowing nobody entered; Exhibition option C and Rover stem are verified.
lessons.questionReview: Pool entry, room approval and photo consent separate needing a condition from being guaranteed the outcome. The radio and key questions combine only-if constraints.

lessons.title: Reverse and negate
lessons.observation: An actual gate sound trace and then a flat trace display possible observations from the scanner. The failed-or-missing scan remains an unresolved choice.
lessons.questionReview: No report rules out exactly three goals. A failed audit trail and missing silver sticker transfer the no-result/no-trigger inference.

lessons.title: Catch the false reverse
lessons.observation: The hall door opens under training and then remains open when the booking changes to assembly. This visibly supplies the alternative explanation.
lessons.questionReview: Sour fruit and non-lemons illustrate false reversal and false negation. Red stickers and blue caps test alternate causes under the original one-way rule.

lessons.title: Join matching links
lessons.observation: A visitor takes an actual route from the locked gate to the side entrance and adds a signature in the book. The ordered chain retains its direction.
lessons.questionReview: The sign-in chain works forwards or contrapositively. Badge scanning deliberately leaves a missing link; the museum question supplies a complete chain.

lessons.title: Rewrite the exception
lessons.observation: Both tomorrow scenes now show the same coach present. One ball stays on the equipment counter while the other moves from its counter to the basket. Coach presence leaves collection undecided.
lessons.questionReview: The picnic, coach and concert examples teach unless, provided that and as long as. The fun run and lever questions test both a triggered rule and an undecided case.

lessons.title: Keep every route open
lessons.observation: The 13-point team falls short of the 15-point path while the fair-play route traces to the final. The alternative explains the known final despite the failed threshold.
lessons.questionReview: The badge can come from different sources. The qualification question gives an exhaustive route list; the free-bag question deliberately leaves other routes open.

lessons.title: Notice the strength of words
lessons.observation: The jersey stays within the team region after missed practice. The medical explanation remains an unconfirmed possibility.
lessons.questionReview: Usually and tend to permit exceptions. Practice contrasts a stronger condition that would guarantee a progress card with an allowed late-bus exception.

lessons.title: Judge each speaker
lessons.observation: Rob’s flags come down; Paul’s flags stay up as a banner and people move along the shopfront. Identical displayed flags can accompany the parade.
lessons.questionReview: The robot speakers refer to separate trials. The launch and badge questions require evaluating both speakers independently before choosing the combined verdict.

lessons.title: Break a “must” claim
lessons.observation: Dani changes from last to first while Ava, Ben and Chen retain their relative order on the track.
lessons.questionReview: Dani can stand after Chen without breaking the other clues, defeating one must-claim. Book orders and permissible club choices likewise test all legal cases.

lessons.title: Build one legal world
lessons.observation: Four shop shutters open on Monday, Friday, Tuesday and Thursday, leaving Wednesday shut. This supplies one timetable meeting the rules.
lessons.questionReview: The video tests a proposed complete ordering against the rules. The library opening schedule and four-demonstration transfer each require constructing a permitted case.

lessons.title: Find the contradiction
lessons.observation: The extra car enters an already full three-car park. With the fourth car present, the maximum is broken, and backing a car out restores legality.
lessons.questionReview: A strict upper bound excludes 50. The exhibit pair and runner order questions require identifying a condition every attempt would violate.

lessons.title: Read the quantifier exactly
lessons.observation: The attendance register changes from all present to one absentee and then to all absent. Chen’s cell clears before its new mark, so incompatible marks no longer overlap.
lessons.questionReview: The choir and cards distinguish some, none and not-all. The club and garden questions require following existence without inventing extra members.

lessons.title: Prove it is undecided
lessons.observation: Sam’s independent marker moves above Nina and below Max in two possible orders; Nina, Leo and Max keep their relative heights.
lessons.questionReview: Different legal blue counts give different least-common colours. The race and counter questions look for alternative legal cases with different answers.

lessons.title: Find the missing bridge
lessons.observation: A possible earlier difference changes while the observed later comparison stays fixed. The illustrative graph gives the competing explanation a visible cause.
lessons.questionReview: The club survey supplies evidence, a population claim and a sampling gap. The library-sign and theatre examples ask which information tests the missing bridge.

lessons.title: Support the exact claim
lessons.observation: The groups begin at a comparable baseline, then show different gains on the same spelling test. The chart measures improvement in the intended direction.
lessons.questionReview: Matched shelter and spelling comparisons test the exact claim. Tray size and pre-task silence ask which comparison answers the causal doubt most directly.

lessons.title: Challenge the bridge
lessons.observation: Email reminders and phone calls enter the same point on the same timeline as late arrivals decline. Either intervention may contribute and the observation does not isolate one.
lessons.questionReview: Unsafe routes undercut the cycling proposal even with more racks. Museum attendance and parent workshops test alternative explanations and a missed practical barrier.

lessons.title: Name the faulty step
lessons.observation: A linked trophy and attendance register demonstrate the forward condition. The reverse reading is tested against Noah appearing on the register despite an unproved award.
lessons.questionReview: Silence is poor proof that everyone liked the rule. The workshop sample and limited library search require locating the unjustified leap.

lessons.title: Negate the hidden support
lessons.observation: An extra bicycle moves beside the school rack to show demand. Removing the unmet demand weakens the stated case for another rack.
lessons.questionReview: Negating the presumed accessibility benefit tests the online-interview mechanism. Bottle loans and due-date reminders require a genuinely necessary bridge.

lessons.title: Test the direction of cause
lessons.observation: Two arrows are drawn separately between reading and vocabulary, in opposite directions. The same association can accommodate either story.
lessons.questionReview: The film distinguishes proposed direction, reverse causation, confounding and chance. Training drills and volunteer/event data check direction and third factors.

lessons.title: Who is missing?
lessons.observation: The chess-club pupils enter a separate sample while the rest of the school remains outside. The selected group is visibly narrower than the proposed population.
lessons.textbookObjective: Sample & Generalisation - WHO/HOW MANY/HOW CHOSEN/WHO MISSING
lessons.questionReview: A large voluntary poll can still miss groups. Evening pool visitors and proposed lunch-menu sampling plans test who answered, how they were selected and whom they represent.

lessons.title: Compare on the same basis
lessons.observation: The 40 and 20 cases are placed over 4,000 and 1,000 respectively; normalising to 100 yields 1 and 2. The outcome reverses the raw count comparison.
lessons.questionReview: Crash totals are adjusted for trips; classes are compared at similar starting points. Rental faults and score gains test denominators and fair comparisons.

lessons.title: Separate sightings from reality
lessons.observation: 113 red and 15 green sightings stay in the notebook while an explicitly hypothetical pond holds two of each. A magnifier makes the concealed green frogs visible without claiming actual population totals.
lessons.questionReview: Changed incident reporting need not mean prevalence changed. Camera availability, survey effort and changed logging thresholds all alter detection.

lessons.title: Order without guessing
lessons.observation: A fourth runner can physically enter between Ava and Ben while Ava stays ahead of Ben and Chloe.
lessons.questionReview: An extra runner can intervene without changing relative order. Both practice chains ask which relationship must survive across orders.

lessons.title: Keep the block together
lessons.observation: The brace forms a three-runner block. The fourth runner moves outside it while the internal spacing holds.
lessons.questionReview: Overlapping immediate-neighbour clues lock three positions together. Cards and task sequences require preserving both direction and adjacency.

lessons.title: Positions and exact gaps
lessons.observation: The fixed black box at 5 anchors a marker which traces two separate leftward hops to the white box at 3.
lessons.questionReview: A fixed endpoint anchors exact step counts. Boxes and bins require tracing exact offsets, including the extra step across an intervening object.

lessons.title: Seats and viewpoints
lessons.observation: The opposite and adjacent seats fill before the four-person seating plan rotates, preserving opposite pairs. In the answer, Ava faces south and east is on her left.
lessons.questionReview: The circular diagram fixes an anchor and changes viewpoint. Inward- and outward-facing seating questions test whose left or right matters.

lessons.title: Solve a timetable
lessons.observation: Music fills Tuesday morning, Art Monday afternoon and Chess the remaining Monday morning. A separate hall schedule excludes the afternoon-only event.
lessons.questionReview: The timetable places fixed dayparts before less restricted events. The two practice schedules combine fixed bookings with relative precedence.

lessons.title: Link the layers
lessons.observation: The ownership tag and colour tags move distinctly onto their locker numbers. The quiz reaches the left edge when trying Ava in locker 1.
lessons.questionReview: Number, colour and name occupy separate layers of one locker diagram. The locker and desk questions force a new ownership/colour match.

lessons.title: When one clue is enough
lessons.observation: The shared first position leaves both rows. Cara-before-Ben retires the first row. The transfer question gives the opposite constraint and retains the other row.
lessons.questionReview: An extra constraint must leave a single valid order. The four-person practice queues ask which one added fact determines all positions.

lessons.title: Matching by elimination
lessons.observation: The compass flies to Noah, torch to Kai and camera to Mila. The pet question assigns the dog to Ana after the other constraints.
lessons.questionReview: A confirmed item removes the other cell possibilities. An expedition, pets, carried objects and instruments all use one-to-one elimination.

lessons.title: What does or allow?
lessons.observation: Each switch pair is visible separately. Both-on and both-off fail exactly-one, while in the inclusive pen question only both-off fails.
lessons.questionReview: The truth table contrasts inclusive or with exactly one. Team selections and coloured chips combine those quantifiers with other rules.

lessons.title: Find what every case shares
lessons.observation: Each case draws its own implication to Nina or Omar. Their possible other outcome remains possible. The quiz separately follows the bell/lamp cases.
lessons.questionReview: Branch on the two cases and trace their shared consequence. Different route items both force a guide; both team branches force Quin.

lessons.title: Use the answer options
lessons.observation: Cara–Ava–Ben satisfies each rule in turn. In the proposed transfer order the first rule fails and Cara remains in the middle.
lessons.questionReview: One violated clue eliminates a row; every condition must hold to retain one. Display and shipping schedules test candidate options against all rules.

lessons.title: Count truths, not confidence
lessons.observation: Enumerated winner rows visibly yield one false statement only for Cara. The second board tests truth instead and yields two true only for blue.
lessons.questionReview: Count actual truth values for every candidate. The prize, token boxes and number questions require exactly the requested number true or false.

lessons.title: Sets and real members
lessons.observation: A witness dot lands inside the musician/dancer overlap outside the excluded group. The separate swimmer enclosure is marked as potentially empty.
lessons.questionReview: Trace a real person across set inclusions and exclusions without assuming a universal rule creates members. Guide/artists and keeper/volunteers supply a real witness.

lessons.title: Ask a decisive question
lessons.observation: Testing below 20 produces the two separate pairs 12/13 and 24/34. The last-digit question then produces one code in each tray.
lessons.questionReview: Both yes and no answers must settle the target. Trip cases ask for the map owner only; the code question asks for its first digit only.

lessons.title: Trace the whole route
lessons.observation: A new bridge joins the two existing route components; the marker traverses the connected path. The quiz analog joins B to C.
lessons.questionReview: A route requires a continuous sequence of permitted links. The two practice graphs require bridging separate components and respecting one-way links.

lessons.title: Track a reflection
lessons.observation: The marked shape crosses a vertical mirror and the high dot stays high. A separate half-turn moves it low, which answers the prediction. In the final transparent-sheet example the upper-left, right-facing key becomes upper-right and left-facing. Its tooth still points down.
lessons.questionReview: A high dot on an L is reflected and contrasted with a half-turn. The recap fixes a copper top edge and moves to the underside of a transparent sheet. Coordinate questions test vertical/horizontal reflection including arrow direction.

lessons.title: Turn the whole shape
lessons.observation: The rigid shape turns about a fixed pin and carries its dot from upper left to upper right. The half-turn prediction instead lands lower right.
lessons.questionReview: Track the rigid shape and marked point about a fixed centre. The two coordinate questions vary angle, starting direction and rotation centre.

lessons.title: Views of cube stacks
lessons.observation: Moving projection collapses depth to show column maxima 2,3,2. The corrected answer at 4.1 and 11.6 s shows a fully visible rectangle of six square ground cells.
lessons.questionReview: The front silhouette takes per-column maxima; the overhead footprint counts occupied cells. Practice checks front and right projections of new stacks.

lessons.title: Unfold one step at a time
lessons.observation: Folds reverse one at a time. D1 reflects into A1, then the side fold gives D4/A4. The final board shows all four. A hole on a crease produces only two distinct positions.
lessons.questionReview: Undo crease reflections in reverse and count distinct points. Both off-crease and on-crease punches are represented in the questions.

lessons.title: Fold a cube net
lessons.observation: Six square panels stay hinged while the net closes. The far flap E finishes opposite C. The other pairs A/F and B/D account for all six. The visible A/D/E corner agrees with the net.
lessons.questionReview: Fold a cross-shaped net into fixed opposite pairs and a three-face corner. The practice nets change their lettering and layout.

lessons.title: The same cube—or a mirror?
lessons.observation: The moving die keeps the single pip uppermost with 3 rotating to the front and 5 to the right. On the corrected board, captions remain below both dice.
lessons.questionReview: A rigid die preserves opposite pairs and the handed order of its adjacent faces. A numbered die and lettered cube test two in-plane spins.

lessons.title: Fit the missing piece
lessons.observation: The bent tile moves into all three empty squares. The straight comparison still overlaps and leaves a gap; its separate 90-degree rotation preserves straightness.
lessons.questionReview: Counting area precedes a test of outline, bends and permissible rotation. The two grid problems require filling the exact remaining cells.

lessons.title: Keep operations in order
lessons.observation: Arrow cards exchange positions on separate arcs below the title before the designated outer arrows turn. The quiz gives Q-right, P-left, R-down.
lessons.questionReview: Apply swaps or translations first, then interpret the next rotation in the updated position. Both practice sequences change the initial state.

lessons.title: Separate movement from facing
lessons.observation: The marker travels east from the library, then north from the park. A diagonal joins the start and finish. The separate compass stays fixed while turning west to north.
lessons.questionReview: The route distinguishes destination from orientation. Practice independently tests a net displacement and a turn/walk sequence.

lessons.title: Keep the code consistent
lessons.observation: Letters are placed using the same key in four successive MOON positions; its two O positions agree.
lessons.questionReview: The same letter retains the same symbol at every occurrence. The BEE/BED and PAPER transfers require recovering mappings and reusing them.

lessons.title: Turn clues into positions
lessons.observation: C locks into first position. R is forbidden in second, leaving A to fill it and R to fill third.
lessons.questionReview: Fixed, present-but-misplaced and absent clues constrain positions; the film also warns about copy count. Follow-up codes require one-to-one slot elimination.

lessons.title: Anchor the repeating cycle
lessons.observation: Six intact four-colour groups terminate at position 24; the next two beads put blue at position 26.
lessons.questionReview: A complete cycle and its remainder locate a distant position. Following removal or moving from a non-first starting point tests indexing.

lessons.title: Find the fixed display fault
lessons.observation: Requested 8 and 9 feed corresponding damaged readouts. The upper-left and middle contacts remain off on both; the moving tester identifies precisely those contacts.
lessons.questionReview: Two fixed failed bars must explain multiple digits. The fresh and delayed cases reconstruct which segments work or fail from actual displays.

lessons.title: Track each feature separately
lessons.observation: Arrow moves along four distinct corners and changes dot count on consecutive moves; location and count can be read independently.
lessons.questionReview: Track corner/colour, direction/size and dot counts separately. Whole-state recurrence is distinguished from a single feature returning.

lessons.title: Turn the whole message
lessons.observation: The outer digits in 168 exchange positions before the 6/9 mapping resolves 891.
lessons.questionReview: A whole-message half-turn reverses position order as well as transforming each glyph. Both practice items state the symbol convention explicitly.

lessons.title: Put events on a timeline
lessons.observation: A dated marker runs from Tuesday to Friday, then seven more days to Friday in week two.
lessons.questionReview: Distinguish dates, intervals and event counts. A repeating clinic appointment with cancellation and a delayed trip require explicit timelines.

lessons.title: Keep the rate units
lessons.observation: Five tubs are filled jointly per hour. A fills three and the same interval leaves two for B.
lessons.textbookObjective: Rate / Speed / Relative Rate / Combined Rate
lessons.questionReview: Steady water rates add; a chase uses the difference and whole-trip average speed is total distance over time. Practice adds a drain and a counted rest.

lessons.title: Find one equal-sized part
lessons.observation: Counters move into two red and three blue equal groups; four counters per group produce eight red and twelve blue.
lessons.questionReview: The video parts model and common denominator comparison handle both ratio and fraction. Practice changes the mix before asking for a new ratio or share.

lessons.title: Find the resource that runs out
lessons.observation: Eighteen pencils and 21 stickers divide between kits. Seven kits satisfy both supplies, while the remaining two cannot receive stickers.
lessons.questionReview: Check limiting supply for maximum output and whole-vehicle capacity for minimum transport. Practice varies supplies and reserves passenger seats for adults.

lessons.title: Undo the final step first
lessons.observation: The number machine reverses operations from output 34 to input 18; applying the forward operations checks the original output.
lessons.questionReview: Reverse the number machine one operation at a time; distinguish total distance from displacement. Transfer separately tests reversed operations and walking back.

lessons.title: Count each object once
lessons.observation: Six opponents lists produce 30 team entries. Symmetric pairs collapse into a single upper-triangle register of 15 fixtures.
lessons.questionReview: Count unique unordered pairs and distinguish cuts, pieces, posts and gaps. Tournament cancellations and pre-installed posts change the baseline count.

lessons.title: Put the overlap in first
lessons.observation: Seven counters are placed in the overlap, with 11 and 8 in only one group and 5 outside both, giving population 31.
lessons.questionReview: The overlap is counted exactly once and students in neither group remain in the class. The practice items ask for exactly-one and changed neither-group totals.

lessons.title: Check the interval boundary
lessons.observation: At 12:30, the line intersects the 2- and 3-person intervals. The 4-person interval has not begun. Open endpoints distinguish expiry.
lessons.questionReview: Maximum occupancy depends on eligible intervals at a target time. Explicit inclusive starts and exclusive ends resolve boundary cases in both questions.

lessons.title: Rank the right measure
lessons.observation: Three original score intervals produce lengths 16, 11 and 14. Endpoint numbers disappear as gain bars align on zero. The longest bar is the largest improvement.
lessons.questionReview: Improvement differs from final score. Fastest single swims and an eligibility threshold require choosing the specified ranking rule before comparing.

lessons.title: Split the number blocks
lessons.observation: The typesetter fills one-digit, then two-digit, then three-digit blocks. Nine plus 180 digits leaves 240, enough for 80 pages starting at 100.
lessons.questionReview: Change digit costs at powers of ten; repeated signals coincide on a common multiple. One transfer varies the digit budget and the other adds a clock threshold.

lessons.title: Compare the legal total cost
lessons.observation: Against the 67-card gate, one small pack falls short, two small packs cost $20 and one large pack clears the gate at $18.
lessons.questionReview: Filter to purchases satisfying the entire requirement before comparing total cost. Mixed badge packs and calendar-day passes test alternative legal combinations.

lessons.title: Build the unluckiest legal case
lessons.observation: Three draws preserve distinct colours; the fourth draw then has to repeat a colour.
lessons.questionReview: Make the longest legal sequence missing the target, then add one. Follow-ups distinguish three of any colour from specifically two red counters.

lessons.title: Treat each toggle as a reversal
lessons.observation: The highlighted switch paths lead to named lamps, and each affected binary state reverses when pressed.
lessons.questionReview: Toggle means reverse the current state. Overlapping switches and repeated presses are tested from two nontrivial initial settings.

lessons.title: Start with the smaller type
lessons.observation: The dog park isolates the people’s legs before determining eleven dogs. Eight baseline dogs plus three extra identify the three double-dog owners.
lessons.questionReview: Use fixed totals and the increment from substituting a second type. Dogs and owners, scored puzzles and voucher values all implement the same equations.

lessons.title: Read the chart’s denominator
lessons.observation: Twelve tennis counters stay put while four runners leave the denominator: 12/24 becomes 12/20. The chart sector grows from a half to three fifths.
lessons.questionReview: A changing denominator makes the same count a different share. The pet pie and recycling table/bar question test sector and rate interpretation.

lessons.title: Update one complete state
lessons.observation: Individual marbles leave the giver and enter the recipient. All three counters change from 4,4,4 through 2,6,4 to 2,3,7.
lessons.questionReview: Trace each transfer and conserve the total. The counter cycle uses simultaneous start-of-round counts; the number machine selects exactly one rule at each step.

lessons.title: Choose a distinguishing test
lessons.observation: Seeds are compatible with either species. Eating the berry excludes B; the unobserved alternative remains legal if the bird ignores it.
lessons.questionReview: A shared observation cannot identify one candidate. Robot features and box inspections ask which extra measurements split the remaining possibilities.

lessons.title: Look where a violation could hide
lessons.observation: Cleaner applied as directed leaves a visible stain, giving a counterexample to the guarantee. An untreated comparison cannot test the guarantee.
lessons.textbookObjective: Rule Verification / What Must Be Known
lessons.questionReview: An A-without-B case falsifies a conditional. Missing badge information and parcel records test which cases must be checked for violations.
